Sediment transport under partial ice cover

https://doi.org/10.1234/jfs.2019.0417

Winter regimes on braided northern rivers remain poorly constrained. We instrumented a 4 km reach of the Kalix over three consecutive seasons and recorded bedload flux beneath a partial ice cover. Transport rates diverged sharply from open-water predictions.

The observed hysteresis suggests that ice-induced flow concentration, rather than shear stress alone, governs entrainment during the freeze-up period.
